relations.evidence: The _Flex Index_ feature provides the ability for a SQL++ query to leverage either a global secondary index or full-text index transparently with standard SQL++ syntax, simplifying the application development process.

relations.subject: n1ql:flex-index

cross_component_finding: This page draws an explicit architectural contrast between two index services that Flex Index unifies under one SQL++ syntax: 'a global secondary index (GSI) uses a B-tree structure for fast exact search, whereas full-text search (FTS) uses an inverted index to provide efficient term search.' It also contrasts their availability lifecycles: 'Full-text indexes are online and searchable as soon as they are created. GSI indexes are online and searchable after they have been built' - GSI has the staged scheduled/building/online lifecycle that index-state models, but FTS per this page has no equivalent staged lifecycle at all.

notable_absence.finding: The page's Search-index setup walkthrough refers to an 'Advanced' settings panel in the Capella Web Console's index-creation screens - 'click the **Advanced** heading to display the Advanced settings panel' - which is textually identical to the registry's ui-mode:advanced label, but this is a different, unrelated UI affordance (the FTS index's default-analyzer setting), not the query-statement-level Advanced UI gate that ui-mode:advanced models. Not linked, to avoid false conflation between two same-named but unrelated 'Advanced' UI panels.
